steps.text: I will structure the answer: first the circular-economy principle in the business model, then three concrete, verifiable examples drawn from Contoso's public materials.
The sources show three recurring levers: product-as-a-service, recycled-content use, and a take-back system. I will summarise these as examples.

contoso/sustainability_summary.answer:
Contoso embeds circular economy at three points in its business model:

1) Product-as-a-Service: Contoso's printer and battery systems are leased in a pay-per-use model rather than sold — ownership and end-of-life recovery stay with the manufacturer.

2) Recycled-content use: since 2026, 62% of housing parts consist of certified post-consumer recyclate; the 2028 target is 80%.

3) Take-back system: over 4,200 collection points accept end-of-life devices; tested modules are fed back into production.

Conclusion: at Contoso, circularity is not just PR but part of the revenue model (service contracts) and procurement (recyclate quota).

contoso/esg_check.answer:
ESG check — Contoso (based on published disclosures):

Emissions — GOOD: Scope 1/2 reported quarterly; SBTi target is registered. GAP: Scope 3 categories 4–11 only partially covered; sub-suppliers are almost entirely missing.

Supply chain — GAP: Tier-1 suppliers are audited, but the deeper Tier-2/3 level has no published failure rate or corrective actions.

Governance — GOOD: ESG KPIs are linked to executive compensation; the report follows the CSRD structure.

Biggest gap: Scope 3 depth and supply-chain transparency beyond the Tier-1 level.

contoso/supply_chain_dashboard.answer:
Supply-chain dashboard for Contoso (automated):

Data sources:
1) Supplier portal: Tier-1/2 submit monthly emissions and audit data via a secured API.
2) ERP extraction: production and logistics data from SAP/Contoso ERP via a nightly job.
3) Public Scope 3 data: industry benchmarks added via API.

KPIs: Scope 3 coverage (%), recyclate share per SKU, supplier compliance rate, CO2 per product unit.

Automation: an orchestration job collects, validates and visualises daily; deviations trigger alerts. This turns manual reporting into a live control instrument.

steps.text: I will define the data model, capture and use of the product passport.

steps.query: digital product passport EU regulation 2027 materials recyclate

steps.text: The passport links material, recyclate and repair — readable via QR/NFC across the device lifetime.

contoso/product_passport.answer:
Digital product passport for Contoso devices:

Captured data:
• Material master: metals, plastics, critical raw materials.
• Recyclate share: % per component, certified.
• Repair: exploded view, spare-part availability, repairability score.
• Lifecycle: origin, maintenance, take-back.

Usage: QR/NFC on the device opens the passport; workshops and recyclers read material & disassembly; customers see the sustainability profile. Meets the EU product-passport mandate (from 2027) and closes the circular-reporting loop.

contoso/net_zero_roadmap.answer:
Net-zero roadmap — Contoso to 2035:

Milestones:
• 2027: 100% renewable energy in own operations (Scope 1/2).
• 2030: recyclate quota to 80%, take-back network to 8,000 points.
• 2035: Scope 3 reduction 50% vs. base year; remainder via certified sinks.

Levers: renewable energy, material circularity, electrified logistics, supplier programmes.

Risks: Scope 3 depth (Tier-2/3), raw-material prices, regulation. Controlled via the supply-chain dashboard (see demo).

contoso/stakeholder_report.answer:
Outline — stakeholder sustainability report (CSRD/ESRS):

1) Foreword & strategy (ESRS 2 GOV/SBM)
2) Double-materiality analysis (impact + financial)
3) Environment (E1 climate, E5 resource use/efficiency, E3 water)
4) Social (S1 workforce, S2 supply chain)
5) Governance (G1 conduct, ESG compensation)
6) Metrics & methodology (Scope 1/2/3, recyclate, take-back)
7) Outlook & roadmap

Contoso strongly covers E1/E5; the remaining gap is supply-chain depth (S2), which the report should flag as a priority.
